subtype: Approach: asks several friends for suggestions [Action]
passage: Tejas wanted a name for the village cricket team, and "Team Tejas" did not sound right. After school he sat under the banyan tree with a stub of pencil and a torn page. He asked five friends one by one, and then his cousin Pankaj, who had come for the harvest week. "Thunder Bulls." "Super Sixers." "Dhoop Dhamaka." "Lazy Langurs." And Pankaj said, "Mango Tigers." Tejas wrote all six names in a column and read them out to the group, watching faces. Mango Tigers made everyone laugh, even the boy who had suggested the Bulls. "That's ours," said Tejas, and drew a tiger holding a bat.

qa.q: Who did Tejas ask besides five friends?
qa.a: Tejas also asked his cousin Pankaj.

qa.q: How did Tejas feel about the name "Team Tejas" at the start?
qa.a: Tejas felt it did not sound right, so he was not satisfied and wanted a name that everyone would like.

qa.q: What could Tejas do if two names got equal laughs?
qa.a: Tejas could ask the players to vote by raising hands, so the team decides together.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel when Mango Tigers was chosen?
qa.a: Pankaj may feel proud and happy, since Pankaj's idea was picked.

grounding: Shows a boy asking five friends and a cousin for team names, writing them all down and choosing the one that made everyone laugh.
